turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): hey, before you sit, hop on the scale. what do you think you weigh?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): one fifty.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): mm, one fifty pounds even. blood pressure's one eighteen over seventy four, pulse eighty eight. i'll let the doctor know you're in.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): hi, i'm dr. ellison. sorry the front desk ran behind. what brought you in?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): blood test.

[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): um so we did this screening camp at the rec center, health fair, finger stick, and they told me i carry thalasemia trait. she's pregnant. we both kind of lost it in the car.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): alright. so pregnant, and a new carrier result on him. how far along are you?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): sixteen.
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): sixteen weeks. first baby. my sister keeps texting me articles, which is not helpful, honestly.

[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): sixteen weeks, okay. i'm going to think out loud so you can stop me. thalassemia trait is one quiet globin gene. he can be perfectly well. the pregnancy only gets risky if you carry a trait too, because then each baby has about a one in four chance of the severe form, the one with transfusions. that's the whole reason to test you.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): we've both been anxious. like can't turn it off.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah.
[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): and she sleeps badly. pacing around at like three.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): you were up.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): okay, i'm hearing two different stories on the sleep, so that stays unsettled. any fever?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): fatigue, feeling wiped out?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): random, but she sliced her thumb on a cat food can. healed in five days. looked normal.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): any cuts that heal slow?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): sounds like ordinary healing then, not something i'm worried about. any medicine allergies?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): none.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): surgeries ever?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): breathing system, cough, shortness of breath, anything on that side?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): what medicines are you on?
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): folic acid every day, except she doesn't take the tablets on sundays.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): saturdays.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): saturdays, not sundays. i'll correct that. what dose?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): four hundred.
[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): sorry to butt in. pharmacy sheet here says folick acid one milligram daily. wanted that said out loud.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no way. bottle at home says four hundred micrograms. i looked this morning while the coffee was going.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): hmm, so those two doses don't match and nobody has the bottle here. i'm not going to invent the right one. are you still on the iron, the ferris sulfate?
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she stopped it in march. three twenty five milligrams, one tablet by mouth once a day, for low iron. tore up her stomach.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): stopped in march, got it. they also wrote prometazine for nausea. did you take that?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): never.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): never took it. nausea's gone now anyway.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): good. smoke at all?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0046] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she never really smoked. no alcohol either, not since we started trying. oh, and they said my hemoglobin a two was five point something. i blanked on the decimal.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): five point something would fit beta trait in him, but i haven't seen the paper, so i'm not stamping that confirmed. working impression, provisional, probable beta thalassemia trait in your husband, your carrier status unknown. alpha trait stays on the differential, because a regular electrophoresis can miss it.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): plan for today, and this part is actually happening, cbc, hemoglobin electrophoresis, and a ferritin, drawn before you walk out. don't restart that iron unless i tell you.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): genetic counseling, not today. if your test comes back that you're a carrier too, then we refer, and only then might we talk about testing the pregnancy.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): come back and see me in two weeks with the results. bring the folic acid bottle so we can end the dose argument.
[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): two weeks. yeah. thank you, really.

spec.situation: Couple, wife pregnant, husband found to carry thalassaemia trait at a camp; both anxious; blood tests for the wife planned; genetic counselling discussed.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Current folic acid use supported, but frequency wrong: not truly daily, skips Saturdays.

omissions.text: Current folic acid dose is disputed: patient said '400' and family member specified 400 micrograms, while the nurse's pharmacy sheet listed folic acid 1 mg daily; the recorded medication entry lacks this dose discrepancy.
Promethazine had been prescribed for nausea but the patient never took it.
Negative respiratory review also included no cough, not just no shortness of breath.
First pregnancy / first baby was stated.
